modules.title: Introduction to Islamic Ethics and Morality
modules.html:
Truthfulness, honesty, modesty, patience, gratitude and other moral qualities taught by Islam. This section covers introduction to islamic ethics and morality.

Key points

  • A 'Mahr' in an Islamic marriage is the _____. — obligatory gift from husband to wife.
  • Islamic monotheism is divided into three categories: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah, Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, and _____. — Tawhid al-Asma was-Sifat.
  • Islamic monotheism is divided into categories: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah, Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, and _____. — Tawhid al-Asma was-Sifat.
  • The Islamic calendar (Hijri) starts from the year of — Hijrah.

Worked examples

Q: A 'Mahr' in an Islamic marriage is the _____.
A: obligatory gift from husband to wife — Mahr is the mandatory dowry or gift paid by the groom to the bride at the time of marriage as a token of respect and security.

Q: Islamic monotheism is divided into three categories: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah, Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, and _____.
A: Tawhid al-Asma was-Sifat — The third category involves the belief in Allah's unique Names and Attributes as mentioned in the Qur'an and Sunnah.

quiz.q: The Islamic calendar (Hijri) starts from the year of?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Hijrah.

quiz.q: The angel responsible for blowing the trumpet (Sur) to signal the Day of Judgment is _____.
quiz.solution: Israfil is the angel tasked with blowing the trumpet twice: once to end life and once to initiate the resurrection.

quiz.q: The 'Khulafah ar-Rashidun' refers to the _____.
quiz.solution: This title is given to the first four Caliphs: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali, who followed the Sunnah of the Prophet closely.

quiz.q: The legal ruling that is 'highly recommended' but not strictly obligatory is called _____.
quiz.solution: Mustahabb actions are those for which a person is rewarded if performed, but not punished if omitted.

quiz.q: The 'Haram' months in which fighting is prohibited are _____.
quiz.solution: These four months are sacred, and the Qur'an forbids initiating warfare during them.

quiz.q: The 'Sujud as-Sahw' is performed when a person _____.
options: makes a mistake or forgetfulness in prayer
quiz.solution: Two extra prostrations are performed at the end of Salat to compensate for unintentional omissions or additions.

quiz.q: The term 'Tafsir' refers to _____.
quiz.solution: Mufassirun (commentators) use linguistics, history, and Hadith to explain the meanings of Qur'anic verses.

quiz.q: The 'Nisab' for sheep and goats for Zakat starts at _____ animals.
quiz.solution: One must own at least 40 sheep or goats for one full lunar year before Zakat becomes due on them.

quiz.q: The specific Zakat given before the Eid al-Fitr prayer is _____.
quiz.solution: Zakat al-Fitr is a charitable obligation for every Muslim at the end of Ramadan to ensure the poor can celebrate Eid.
